chunks: Sama'ah ibn Mihran asked him about two men who rose and looked toward the dawn. One of them said, "There it is," and the other said, "I do not see anything."
He said: "Then let the one for whom dawn has not become clear eat and drink, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says:"
"And eat and drink until the white thread becomes distinct to you from the black thread of dawn; then complete the fast until the night."

Sama'ah said: And I asked him about a man who ate and drank after dawn had risen in the month of Ramadan. He said: "If he rose and looked, but did not see the dawn, then ate, and afterward looked again and saw the dawn, then he should complete his fast and there is no repetition upon him. But if he rose and ate and drank, then looked toward the dawn and saw that it had risen, then he should complete that fast and make up another day, because he began with eating before looking, so repetition is upon him."

key_terms.الصِّيَامَ: the fast that must be completed until night
key_terms.الْإِعَادَةُ: repetition or making up the fast
key_terms.الْفَجْرُ: true dawn, the point at which fasting begins
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramadan, in which fasting is obligatory
key_terms.يَتَبَيَّنَ: becomes clear and distinct with certainty
key_terms.يَقْضِي: he makes up the missed obligation on another day

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone eats at dawn in Ramadan before being sure that fajr has begun?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the ruling for one who is uncertain whether true dawn has appeared at the start of the fast. It establishes that eating and drinking remain permitted until dawn becomes clear, and it distinguishes between one who checked and reasonably did not see dawn and one who ate before checking, with different legal consequences for each.
